writeup.title: G4WDB Writeup
writeup.subtitle: G4WDB: Gemma 4 War Disaster Buddy Offline
writeup.description: An AI survival assistant for armed conflict zones, designed for the Gemma 4 Good Hackathon. G4WDB delivers offline, privacy-preserving intelligence when cellular infrastructure is destroyed and the internet is absent.
writeup.abstract_text: Over 100 million people currently live in active war zones where communication infrastructure is systematically destroyed, internet access is unavailable, and cloud-based AI assistance is impossible. G4WDB uses Gemma 4 E2B to provide medical triage, UXO recognition, Bluetooth mesh danger mapping, and family reunification entirely on-device.

problem.one: War zones frequently face deliberate destruction of cell towers, long-term blackouts, and no reliable connectivity.
problem.two: Existing cloud AI assistants fail without internet, while static offline manuals cannot answer context-specific questions.
problem.three: No current solution provides privacy-preserving family reunification offline.
problem.four: Conflict-specific threats such as shrapnel injuries, unexploded ordnance, and sniper danger require specialized support.

writeup.solution_intro: G4WDB is optimized for mid-range Android hardware and includes:

solution.one: Gemma 4 E2B (2.6B parameters) quantized to 4-bit with LiteRT for sub-500MB footprint.
solution.two: Silent-mode touch interaction and vibration feedback for tactical safety.
solution.three: Multimodal UXO recognition using onboard camera analysis.
solution.four: Bluetooth mesh danger zone mapping and encrypted family search.
solution.five: Cross-platform support for Android, iOS, Windows, and future VR/AR/XR interfaces.

accessibility.one: High-contrast, large tap targets, and offline localization for inclusive access.
accessibility.two: VR/AR/XR-ready interfaces for training, hazard annotation, and immersive mission planning.
accessibility.three: Support for Windows, iOS, and Android app formats to cover field and command center use cases.

ethics.one: No weaponization: The system cannot identify targets or support offensive operations.
ethics.two: Data privacy by design: medical queries are never stored, camera inputs are processed in RAM only, and danger reports are anonymized.
ethics.three: First-time consent screen clearly explains offline operation, sharing policies, and deletion controls.
